reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the express warranty runs only sixty (60) days from the Effective Date with a hard December 31, 1999 cut-off, which is below the fallback of 90 days for software and, because it runs from the Effective Date rather than delivery/acceptance, can expire at or before acceptance — a material failure of the fallback, not a mere sub-element gap.

Rationale accurately acknowledges the parts that already comply (substantial-conformance warranty, no-malicious-code warranty, correction/replacement/refund remedy ladder, disclaimer limited to implied warranties), so it does not over-claim or double-flag.

Redline is targeted and directionally right: it substitutes 'twelve (12) months from Corio's acceptance of the Software pursuant to Section 3.1' for the 60-day/Effective-Date period and deletes the fixed cut-off, leaving the second (malicious code) sentence, the remedy paragraph and the 'Warranty Period' definition intact and still operative.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic is not substantive here — the only substantive replacement is the duration/trigger language the rule requires be rewritten; the balance of the paragraph is preserved verbatim.
Comment is accurate, in tone, states what changed and why (period could expire before or shortly after delivery), cites the 12-month playbook position and offers the 90-days-from-acceptance fallback.
